statement: Audit context-preserving omission of unused DSpark query work on all-rank unfinished prefill
mechanism: Retain prompt-context KV/anchor and any live confidence/state updates; omit only query outputs and computation with no later consumer.
proposed_change: No runtime patch. First prove live-out semantics on strictly nonfinal chunks across every DEP rank, including idle ranks. Whole query skip is obstructed by adaptive confidence dependencies.
counterevidence: Original aggregate-all-proposals-consumed assertion was too broad: scheduler and V2 input preparation discard unfinished-prefill proposal IDs.
FULL query graph includes required context KV/anchor work; skipping entire replay is incorrect.
Adaptive confidence double buffer exposes prior nonfinal-prefill confidence to future decode budgeting under ordinary sequential lifecycle.
Learned confidence uses parent Markov embeddings; first four draws of a five-token chain remain necessary to compute all confidence outputs.
Query KV writes and EPLB/watermark/callback/RNG side effects require independent liveness proof.
No measured eligible-step frequency or exposed cost; long-output ITL may scarcely benefit.
priorcomparison: Distinct work elimination from C025 faster sampler. C025 modest five-step component gain is opposing materiality evidence; do not transfer its microseconds to this hardware/frequency/terminal-step candidate.

CPUcheck.outcome: Supports ignored-token-output premise but refutes treating all head outputs as unused; model illustrates buffer lifecycle, not actual vLLM execution.
CPUcheck.next: Field/side-effect liveness proof and symbolically verify complete context slot coverage. Preserve learned confidence chain; independently assess whether only final sampler step can be omitted.

evalplan: See R2-03-REVISION.md. Existing agent-p75/Mooncake plus chunk-boundary correctness tests. No new serving workload justified absent exposure gap. Whole skip must pass confidence/cache/RNG parity; any policy change requires explicit separate arm. All GPU tests remain future.
